text:
sophie: Heads-up — noticed a big cost spike in eu-west yesterday evening, looks like GPU ASGs got provisioned twice after a state migration. Anyone who did the workspace split touch the tfstate?

james: I ran a state move to split staging/prod workspaces earlier. pipeline failed midway due to a GH action timeout and I assumed the lock would release.

miguel: Which backend did you move between? same S3 bucket or separate buckets?

james: I moved resources from module.gpu_pool in prod workspace into a new prod-gpu workspace. Backend was supposed to be a different prefix in same bucket (s3://redwood-tfstate-eu/prod vs prod-gpu). I did `terraform state mv` locally and then pushed the workspace change.

lee: That usually works but AWS S3 + DynamoDB locking can be flaky for cross-prefix moves if there's eventual consistency and a lingering lock. Did you see a DynamoDB lock record?

james: infra-bot reported a lock, TTL was 5m, but GH action took ~12m to retry. I forced the job to abort. No manual force-unlock done.

olivia: Current impact: we have two ASGs with same tags in eu-west-1, both attached to k8s autoscaler rules. One was created by the original stack, one by the moved state applying to the new workspace. That doubled GPU capacity and cost.

sophie: Crash course evidence — CloudWatch shows group gpu-prod-01 and gpu-prod-01-1 both active from 18:12 UTC. Billing shows spike at ~18:30. Need to avoid destroying either before reconciling state.

miguel: Quick triage steps I propose: 1) Pause autoscaler or scale-down one ASG to 0 desired temporarily 2) Inspect each workspace state with `terraform state pull` to confirm which resources are referenced 3) Use `terraform import` to re-associate orphaned EC2 instances/ASG into the desired state instead of destroying

lee: Agreed. Also check S3 object versions — if backend versioning enabled we can diff older state file. Don't run `terraform apply` until we know which state is authoritative.

james: I pulled both states: prod workspace still references aws_autoscaling_group.gpu_pool (arn:aws:autoscaling:eu-west-1:...:autoScalingGroupName/gpu-prod-01). prod-gpu workspace references the same logical name because state move copied the resource without renaming. So both think they own the same infra.

sophie: So they are duplicates at cloud level because Terraform recreated resources when it applied in the new workspace — it couldn't move AWS resources across workspaces.

olivia: Actioned mitigation: scaled desired capacity of gpu-prod-01-1 to 0 at 18:45. That reduced immediate cost. We left original gpu-prod-01 active.

james: Next steps I took: 1) stopped any running CI pipelines that might run further applies 2) exported both state files: `terraform state pull > prod.tfstate` and `> prod-gpu.tfstate` 3) diffed them with `jq` to find owner attributes

miguel: For recovery we should: - pick authoritative state (prod.tfstate) - in prod-gpu workspace run `terraform state rm module.gpu_pool.aws_autoscaling_group.gpu_pool` to remove the phantom mapping so the workspace no longer claims it - then run `terraform plan` in prod-gpu to ensure no accidental destroy/apply - afterwards re-enable pipelines with guard rails

lee: Be careful with `state rm` — it only removes tracking, not resources. That's what we want here. But do it from a controlled machine (not CI) and create backups: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-tfstate-eu/prod.tfstate ./prod.tfstate.bak` and the same for prod-gpu.

james: I ran the `state rm` in prod-gpu with a backup and then a `terraform plan` — showed nothing to do. Then ran `terraform refresh` to double-check.

sophie: Good. After that we updated autoscaler rules to point to the remaining ASG and scaled down the duplicate to 0; then terminated the extra instances once no pods were scheduled.

olivia: Root cause recap: human-in-the-loop `terraform state mv` across prefixes in same S3 bucket + CI timeout + lingering dynamo lock = state ownership duplication. The moved resource was not imported into new workspace properly before an apply happened.

miguel: Preventive actions: - update runbook for workspace splits: 1) lock TTL increase in dynamo while doing manual moves 2) perform `terraform state pull` and `terraform state mv` from same machine with stable network 3) avoid CI auto-apply on operations that touch state backend layout - require manual approval for workspace/backend changes - add a pre-apply check in GitHub Action that verifies resource ID ownership across workspaces by pulling states and ensuring no overlap

lee: Also propose adding a quick GitHub Action step for state consistency that runs `terraform state list` for changed modules and compares resource IDs across target workspaces. If overlap found, block the apply and notify infra channel.

james: I'll open a small PR to add the preflight check and update the workspace-split playbook with explicit `force-unlock` guidance. Sorry team, my bad on the timing. :cry:

sophie: No blame — useful lessons. For tracking, file an incident doc? cost team will want numbers.

olivia: I'll create a short incident note with estimated cost delta and link to the state diffs. Also will add the S3 object version IDs for audit.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: pipeline stopped for workspace "prod-gpu" by james at 1767852100.

miguel: One final note: if we ever need to reconcile without downtime, use `terraform import` to associate one of the existing ASGs into the chosen workspace state rather than creating new resources. Keep `plan -out` for review.

lee: Thanks all. I'll add the preflight check to the infra-ci board and tag james for the PR review. :thumbsup:
